laser_and_process: CO2 10.6 um, ~14 us pulses, ~120 um beam, 2.4-5.4 W, 3.5 in/s (~89 mm/s), 1000 ppi, air
characterisation: sheet resistance, Raman, XPS, BET, SEM/TEM, CV (supercapacitors)
measured_results: Rs <35 ohm/sq at 2.4 W threshold, <15 ohm/sq at 5.4 W; BET ~340 m2/g; C 97 at%; areal capacitance >4 mF/cm2 at 20 mV/s in 1 M H2SO4
limitations: different laser (ULS); capacitance in acid electrolyte, not saline
relevance_to_us: benchmarks for Rs and process window; capacitance order of magnitude
engineering_decision_supported: E1 acceptance thinking (Rs tens of ohm/sq is achievable); readout calc: double-layer charging negligible -> bipolar DC pulses acceptable (calc_readout.py)

source: Li et al., Adv Mater 29:1700496 (2017) - LIG in controlled atmospheres
laser_and_process: CO2 laser in O2/air vs Ar/H2 atmospheres
measured_results: contact angle 0 deg (air/O2, superhydrophilic) vs >150 deg (Ar/H2)
limitations: our atmosphere is air; no data on aged surfaces
relevance_to_us: exudate will wet LIG electrodes, and can wick along exposed LIG traces
engineering_decision_supported: all traces outside sensing windows must be sealed (polyimide tape); zone windows sized to define the wetted area

source: Milne et al., Int Wound J 13(6):1309-1314 (2016)
characterisation: spot impedance readings in 5 moisture bands at dressing change (n=30 patients, 588 readings)
measured_results: 44.9 % of changes made in optimum moisture band
limitations: observational; mixed dressings; spot-check device; not an RCT
relevance_to_us: baseline inefficiency figure for the user journey (published evidence)
engineering_decision_supported: quantified before-state (cite as published evidence only)

source: McColl, Cartlidge, Connolly, Int J Surg 5(5):316-322 (2007)
characterisation: 8-point impedance moisture mapping with fluid injection
measured_results: moisture distribution non-uniform; some foam regions dried during constant injection
relevance_to_us: prior art for spatial moisture sensing; motivates measuring spread, not one point
engineering_decision_supported: multi-zone concept is prior art -> novelty limited to change-line placement + LIG process

source: Dressing instructions for use (foam dressings with 2 cm rule; Molnlycke Mepilex Border Flex; 3M Tegaderm silicone foam border)
measured_results: change when exudate approaches ~2 cm from pad edge (some foams); saturated when strike-through reaches 3 edges (Mepilex)
limitations: product-specific; read exact IFU of dressing actually tested
relevance_to_us: defines the change line the strip must detect
engineering_decision_supported: alert zone A placed at the IFU change line of the specific test dressing

source: EN 13726-1:2002 (replaced by EN 13726:2023) - absorbency test methods
limitations: protein-free; free-swell method criticised as non-physiological
relevance_to_us: simulated exudate recipe for bench tests
engineering_decision_supported: E3 uses Solution A (documented recipe) and directional inflow from a centre port, not free swell

source: Dealey C, Cameron J, Arrowsmith M. A study comparing two objective methods of quantifying the production of wound exudate. J Wound Care 15(4):149-153 (2006)
measured_results: 0.10-0.21 g/cm2/24h (2 patients, one method); mean 1.3 g/cm2/24h (one method, 5 patients) - methods disagree
limitations: tiny sample; which value belongs to which method unclear
relevance_to_us: order of magnitude of real exudate rates
engineering_decision_supported: E3 runs at accelerated inflow (documented); real-time rates are 10-100x slower -> state that bench timing is not clinical timing

source: Influence of lasing parameters on morphology and electrical resistance of PI-based LIG, Carbon Letters (2023)
laser_and_process: desktop CO2 laser; power, speed, passes, spot overlap
measured_results: passes and spot overlap reduce Rs; PI brand strongly affects quality; desktop unit limited by speed control and thermal management
relevance_to_us: process variability is real; film brand is a variable
engineering_decision_supported: record film brand/lot in every E1 row; keep one roll for all experiments

source: Design of experiments and optimization of LIG (UCC Cork, 2023)
laser_and_process: CO2 laser engraver; power x speed DoE
measured_results: Rs minima at (70 mm/s, 2.1 W) and (340 mm/s, 3.4 W); minima do not follow constant power/speed ratio
engineering_decision_supported: E1 brackets power AND speed around the reference rather than assuming a P/v rule

source: (Authors not recorded) CW CO2 LIG fluence study (2024)
relevance_to_us: contact resistance to LIG is significant
engineering_decision_supported: transmission-line (3-length) test separates contact from material resistance

source: softsolder.com CO2 tube current vs PWM measurements (2022)
measured_results: below ~25 % PWM current is spiky with little difference between settings
relevance_to_us: our '12' sits in the low-PWM range
engineering_decision_supported: E1 logs tube current per setting and repeats the reference on 2 days

characterisation: OCP, DPV, EGFET in buffer, wound-simulating medium, agar
measured_results: pH -54 mV/pH (buffer) falling to -26 mV/pH on agar
relevance_to_us: LIG wound sensors exist in labs; sensitivity drops in realistic media
engineering_decision_supported: do not claim chemical sensing; moisture-front sensing is physically simpler

characterisation: impedance, temperature, ES in mouse wounds
relevance_to_us: closed-loop therapy is prior art and out of our reach
engineering_decision_supported: therapy deferred; scope = moisture-front indication only

engineering_decision_supported: freedom-to-operate check needed; our contribution must be the wound-dressing change-line use + validation, not the strip itself
